fieldValues.title: The Address is core; `AttentionState` stays a cursor
fieldValues.decision_rationale: Addressability and federation are foundational (owner). Cross-repository links are relations, and a core relation cannot rest on an optional extension. The cursor holds a pointer to an Address; it is not the Address (owner), as the concept record already says.
fieldValues.decision_statement: The Address moves to the core (Foundation group) with an optional `repositoryId`; `AttentionState` stays in `ext:addressability` unchanged.
fieldValues.decision_scope: Where the Address is defined (core, Foundation group, instead of ext:addressability), its repositoryId component, the optional containerId, and Address equality; AttentionState stays in ext:addressability unchanged.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Keep the Address in ext:addressability (a core relation would rest on an optional extension). Merge the cursor into the Address (the concept record forbids merging them).
fieldValues.accepted_costs: 14 records change for the move (Integration table, rows 1–14); `ext:addressability` narrows to the cursor; one tightening ([R0], `fieldId` needs `recordId`) with no stored data affected.
evidence_refs: srs-programme conversation container ec40e5ab (the owner's words, 2026-10-30 to 2026-11-02)
fieldValues.review_trigger:
1. Step 2's relation needs an Address the union cannot express, such as a definition (Type, Field) in another repository, which no space covers. *Checked at:* the cross-repository relations RFC.
2. A core construct needs a cursor, not an Address, to cross repositories. *Checked at:* the cross-repository relations RFC and any conversation-layer RFC.
3. The cursor turns out unusable without parts of the Address it no longer gets from its extension. *Checked at:* srs-rust's `attention_service.rs`, the one implementation of `AttentionState`, when it is next changed.
